findings.title: Authenticate update bytes before replacing the trusted executable
findings.evidence: main.go:113-129 passes the HTTP discovery endpoint to updateClient. discovery.go:139-151 constructs HTTP URLs from untrusted DNS-SD addresses; coordinator IDs are public preferences, not authentication keys (coordinator-discovery.ts:69). main.go:155-177 downloads both the archive and its checksum from that same unauthenticated endpoint. update.go:147-170 checks only ELF structure and architecture before replacement. A LAN attacker can impersonate the selected public coordinator ID or alter HTTP responses and supply a matching checksum plus an attacker-controlled ARM64 ELF. The next client launch executes those bytes with the installed client's privileges. HTTPS/WSS pairing does not protect this separate update path.
findings.required_fix: Require authenticated update provenance before replacement. Reuse setup-provisioned TLS trust for update delivery, or verify a bundle signature against a key provisioned through trusted setup. Keep DNS-SD as address discovery only. Refuse update when no trusted identity is configured; a checksum fetched alongside the archive is insufficient. Add rejection coverage for a forged coordinator serving an otherwise valid executable and matching checksum.
